references.text: The Egyptians mourned for Jacob for seventy days, reflecting the same tradition of a longer mourning period for significant figures.
The whole congregation of Israel mourned for Aaron for thirty days, just as they mourned for Moses during that same time period.
Joseph held seven days of mourning for his father Jacob, illustrating Israelite mourning customs.
The men of Jabesh-Gilead fasted for seven days after Saul's death, reflecting mourning traditions in Israel.
David and his men mourned, wept, and fasted until evening over Saul and Jonathan, showing national grief over leaders.
Moses instructed Aaron and his sons about periods of mourning, which is relevant to understanding the mourning time for Moses himself.
